name: Earth
lesson: The earth bears injury without abandoning its course. Mountains and trees add a second lesson: spend your strength for the good of others.

name: Air
lesson: Air moves among many places without taking on their qualities. The wanderer learns to meet changing circumstances without being owned by attraction or aversion.

name: Sky
lesson: Clouds and weather pass through the open sky without marking it. The account uses that spaciousness to contemplate the self beyond passing changes.

name: Water
lesson: Clear water refreshes and purifies. The learner is invited to be gentle in speech and a beneficial presence to others.

name: Fire
lesson: Fire receives what is offered yet is not defined by it. Its hidden and visible forms become an image for inward strength and the self within varied appearances.

name: Moon
lesson: The moon appears to wax and wane, while the text distinguishes it from those changing phases. So, it says, the body's stages do not exhaust the self.

name: Sun
lesson: The sun draws up water and gives it back in rain without keeping it. Reflections in many waters also prompt a meditation on one reality appearing in many forms.

name: Pigeon
lesson: A pigeon family is caught in a hunter's net. This long warning story concerns attachment that overwhelms discernment, within a teaching addressed to a renunciant.

name: Python
lesson: The python waits for what comes rather than chasing every meal. The ascetic lesson is contentment with what is available, not a general instruction to neglect bodily needs.

name: Ocean
lesson: Rivers fill the ocean and seasons alter their flow, yet its depth remains. The learner seeks steadiness through abundance and scarcity.

name: Moth
lesson: Drawn to a flame, the moth is consumed. The image warns of sight and desire outrunning judgment.

name: Bee
lesson: A bee gathers nectar from many flowers; the seeker may draw the essence from many teachings. The passage also warns that storing too much can become a trap.

name: Elephant
lesson: The elephant's attraction leads into captivity. In this male renunciant setting, the example warns about being governed by sensual craving.

name: Honey gatherer
lesson: Someone else takes the honey that bees have stored. The lesson questions accumulation so consuming that its owner never uses or shares it.

name: Deer
lesson: A deer enchanted by a hunter's music is caught. The story asks the seeker to notice when a pleasing sound becomes a lure.

name: Fish
lesson: The fish takes bait and meets the hook. For the Avadhuta, taste is one more sense that can command the mind when left unexamined.

name: Pingala
lesson: Pingala waits anxiously for a paying visitor. When she lets go of that expectation and turns inward, she finally rests; the source gives her change of heart its own extended voice.

name: Kurara bird
lesson: Other birds harass a kurara carrying a piece of meat. Releasing it ends the struggle: possession can cost more peace than it brings.

name: Child
lesson: A child at play is unconcerned with praise or insult. The Avadhuta sees freedom from anxious self-importance.

name: Maiden
lesson: While preparing food for guests, a young woman removes noisy bangles until one remains on each wrist. The Avadhuta draws a lesson about quiet solitude from her practical decision.

name: Arrow maker
lesson: An artisan is so intent on shaping an arrow that a passing king goes unnoticed. Focus makes even an ordinary craft a teacher of attention.

name: Snake
lesson: A snake takes shelter in a place made by another creature. The wandering ascetic sees a way to travel lightly and avoid becoming bound to building a home.

name: Spider
lesson: A spider spins a web from itself and later draws it back. The text uses this image for the divine manifestation and withdrawal of the world.

name: Wasp and captive insect
lesson: The tale of an insect absorbed in fear of a wasp becomes a metaphor for the shaping power of sustained attention. It is a spiritual image, not a zoological claim.
